title: An Approach to Variable Clustering: K-means in Transposed Data and its Relationship with Principal Component Analysis
summary: The paper addresses the underexplored link between PCA and K-means when K-means clusters variables rather than observations. It standardizes the data, applies PCA to obtain loadings, transposes the standardized matrix, runs K-means on variables, and quantifies each variable cluster's contribution to each principal component as S_{k,j} and normalized P_{k,j}. On USArrests with K=2, the Murder/Assault/Rape cluster has S_{2,PC1}=1.662, dominating PC1, which explains 62.5% of variance.

match_target.why: It is the paper's central USArrests result and the user's target: a single PCA plus K-means on a 50x4 dataset, no training or heavy compute, and it directly verifies the S_{2,PC1}=1.662 contribution.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: no repeated-run std is reported, and S_{2,PC1} is a numeric contribution rather than an accuracy/F1/AUC score; use 10% relative tolerance.

requirements.stmt: Standardize each variable using its mean and sample standard deviation (n-1 denominator) before PCA.
requirements.quote: The scaled (normalized) data set Z with zij ∈Z, is obtained by the transformation:

requirements.stmt: Apply PCA to the standardized matrix Z and obtain the loading matrix L.
requirements.quote: PCA is applied to the Z matrix to find a linear transformation that projects the data into a new lower dimensional space, maximizing the retained variance.

requirements.stmt: Construct the absolute-loading matrix La from L.
requirements.quote: Let La be the matrix of absolute loadings, where La = |ljk| (|ljk| ∈L).

requirements.stmt: Transpose the standardized data matrix Z to get ZT of size p x n.
requirements.quote: Let ZT be the transposed matrix of Z, of dimension p × n.

requirements.stmt: Use K=2 for USArrests, as reported from the elbow method.
requirements.quote: In USArrests, two clusters were obtained by means of the elbow method

requirements.stmt: Run Euclidean K-means on the transposed standardized data ZT, minimizing within-cluster squared distances.
requirements.quote: The objective of K-means is to partition the transposed data set ZT into K clusters

requirements.stmt: For USArrests K=2, obtain C1={UrbanPop} and C2={Murder, Assault, Rape}.
requirements.quote: Cluster 2 C2 groups the variables Murder, Assault and Rape; Cluster 2 C1 contains the variable UrbanPop.

requirements.stmt: Compute S_{k,j} as the sum of absolute PCA loadings of variables in cluster k on component j.
requirements.quote: The contribution Sk,j of each cluster k to each principal component j is calculated as the sum of the absolute loadings

requirements.stmt: Compute P_{k,j} by dividing S_{k,j} by the sum of S over all clusters for the same component j.
requirements.quote: The contribution ratio Pk,j of each cluster k to each principal component j is calculated as:

requirements.stmt: Check that proportions sum to 1 for each principal component.
requirements.quote: The sum of the proportions for each principal component must equal 1 (or 100%).

requirements.stmt: Return both the S contribution matrix and the P proportion matrix.
requirements.quote: Ensure: Contributions Sk,j and proportions Pk,j of each cluster to each principal component

requirements.stmt: Set a fixed random seed for K-means reproducibility.
requirements.quote: Once the number of clusters is defined, the K-means algorithm is run, ensuring reproducibility by setting a fixed value for the random seed.

requirements.stmt: Use absolute loadings when accumulating cluster contributions, regardless of loading sign.
requirements.quote: we use the absolute values of the loads because we are interested in the magnitude of the influence
